key_insight: Auxiliary-space multigrid preconditioners remove the need for nested conforming coarse meshes by building the hierarchy through arbitrary mesh agglomeration.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers robust preconditioning for conforming finite element systems on general domains where constructing conforming coarse meshes is difficult.
method: Couple fine-mesh conforming Lagrange elements to coarse polytopal DG or hybrid high-order discretisations.
Transfer coarse solutions by element-wise interpolation and nodal averaging, with local potential reconstruction for the hybrid high-order variant.
Apply multigrid on further agglomerated meshes using point-Jacobi or vertex-star additive Schwarz smoothing.
evidence_signal: Condition-number bounds scale as O((H/h)^3), improving to O((H/h)^2) for DG with appropriately scaled penalties; 2D and 3D tests on structured and unstructured meshes confirm robustness.
watch_item: The bounds worsen with the coarsening ratio H/h, so aggressive agglomeration may reduce preconditioner effectiveness.
paper_title: Geometric Multigrid Preconditioners for conforming Finite Element Methods on Arbitrarily Agglomerated Meshes
